answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a bonded claim is proven fraudulent. The lock does not reveal whether two accounts share an owner, so it is not perfect Sybil resistance; it makes influence costly: splitting into many identities requires capital for every one, tied up and at risk. A sable trader may cross a glacier route past cedar depots, but cannot multiply voting weight for free.
